podcast.title: 1950s Greenwich Village Singer
podcast.body: Connie Converse was a singer on the Ascense in the 1950s, gaining recognition within the Beat Nick crowd in Greenwich Village. Despite her talent, her career didn't flourish as she had hoped. "The Converse was a singer on the Ascense in the 1950s, making her name with the Beat Nick Crowd and Greenwich Village."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 9: The Disappearance of Richey Edwards

podcast.title: Disappearance Amidst Depression
podcast.body: When her music career failed to take off, Connie Converse moved to Michigan and fell into a deep depression. On her 50th birthday, she penned a series of farewell letters, declaring her intention to seek a "new life," before walking away from her home and never being seen again. "On her 50th birthday, she wrote a series of farewell letters saying that she was going to search for a new life. She walked away from that home in Michigan and was never seen again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
